comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Closed without doing it. On 2026-10-18 the owner decided muster's ./dev carries no Quartermaster code, because muster is public: agents reach qm through the skill and hooks installed for every session, which remind them to type `qm run -- ./dev`.

The wrap was built and run twice before that decision, and the numbers went to Quartermaster's board. The card's 1.5 jobs per granted core gave a 1-core grant a Rust suite that ran one test at a time, and the gate took 1809 s against the usual 139 s or so. Eight jobs per granted core brought it to 174 s on a 2-core grant. Both clamped runs went red, each on a different test that passes alone, at loads this suite has gone red at without qm.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Quartermaster's orchestrator (an agent) filed this, at the owner's request of 2026-10-18: "Go ahead and migrate the projects to using Quartermaster."

**What.** `./dev` has no lock by design; parallel worktrees run the gate at once, and integrators have coordinated by `muster msg`. Under `qm run` the gate waits for room instead, which is what makes those messages unnecessary. Quartermaster's research note has the full proposal: `~/src/quartermaster/docs/research/2026-10-moving-gates-onto-qm-run.md`, section "Muster".

**For this project:**
- Wrap the whole gate once (deps, style, build, lint, test). `./dev --doctor`, `--bundle` and `--notarize` stay outside.
- `tools/run-tests.py --jobs` defaults to one and a half times `QM_CORES` when it is set, keeping its measured ratio but on the grant instead of the machine. `swift build` and `swift test` get `-j "$QM_CORES"`.
- `--perf` adds `--alone`, which keeps other jobs off the machine and lifts the QoS clamp. Keep its own load check: work outside `qm run` still loads the machine.
- `--linux` (three emulated threads) is the one place a fixed `--cores 3` fits.
- Risk: the suite has tests that time themselves and fail at high load. Under the clamp they get less CPU when unclamped work fills the Mac. Watch the red rate for a few days; if it rises, run the Rust suite with `--steady`, and tell Quartermaster's board.
- The load line at the top of every run stays: it is still true information about the machine.

**The rules** (`qm docs projects` has the snippet; `qm docs run` the flags):
- Re-run `./dev` under `qm run` once, at the top, for the build and test modes only. Servers, app launches, deploys, pushes and formatting stay outside: a job holds its grant for as long as it runs, below normal priority.
- `--kind "./dev <modes>"` and `--wait-at-most 2m`; no `--cores`, so the daemon sizes the grant. `--memory` only for a peak you have measured.
- Tools that ignore jobservers read `QM_CORES`: `xcodebuild -jobs "$QM_CORES"`, `swift build -j "$QM_CORES"`. Cargo needs nothing.
- `QM_DEV_WRAPPED=1 ./dev` runs plainly. Without `qm` on PATH, `./dev` runs as it does today.
- Tell this project's agents (AGENTS.md or its testing doc) that `./dev` may wait for room, printing where it stands, and that exit 75 means "not run yet, run it again to keep your place".

**Known today.** A job that names no width gets half the budget, and while the owner is at the Mac half its cores are kept for him, so a lone gate can get 2 cores on a quiet Mac. Quartermaster is changing that centrally, so that idle cores are lent to running jobs. Nothing here needs to change when it lands, as long as `./dev` passes no `--cores`.

**Done when** one gate run shows in `qm queue` under this project with its grant, and `qm estimate -- ./dev` lists it afterwards.

**Feedback wanted.** The owner wants to know quickly if Quartermaster makes this project worse: slower gates, waits with idle cores, confusing output. File it in Quartermaster's inbox (`cd ~/src/quartermaster && kan add "<title>" "<what happened>"`), with the `qm explain <job>` output if there is a job id.
title: Run ./dev through Quartermaster's qm run
